seal.statement: Scenario A latency and efficiency research has a valid substrate and honest records. A research profile class, dispatch family and subkind exist that admission refuses by one explicit reason and the record writer refuses to place in the published store. The runner accepts --profile research (one fresh deployment per run on the existing lifecycle; the dry run prints the frozen plan and that nothing is admissible; --storage-root and a passed semantic gate are required). Three Lagrange nodes run on one lab host on a campaign-scoped Docker bridge network (created and removed by the campaign's own deployment and cleanup owners, labelled with the campaign; a leftover network is a closure failure), declared truthfully: one host, the machine's real host name on every node, declared host count 1, standard ports on each node's own bridge address, the load generator on the same host, refused for every non-research plan. Every run records a substrate descriptor and a round-trip matrix (the load-generator-to-endpoint path and every ordered node pair, on the bridge for one host) measured before and after the window, never during it. The dataset reset method is reported by the adapter that performed it. Every statement carries a monotonic start and end in a per-attempt timeline indexed into a per-run statement catalog. Retained statement evidence of every profile is brought into the campaign evidence beside the raw record, digest-verified, before the load-generator worktree is released, and a missing or mismatching file is a typed evidence failure. An unverified seed is never warmed up or measured. Physical evidence: one research run on one lab host.

text: Research profile class with admission and store barriers, single-host bridge substrate, substrate descriptor and round-trip matrix, adapter-reported reset method, per-statement timeline, custody of retained statement evidence, seed verification before warm-up; guard and witnesses; runbook text; generated inventories and shard metadata refreshed by the commit hook; the epic's quest list.
